title: "Projr remote compatibility inventory"
---

Source audit, 23 October 2026. Pinned R source:
[SATVILab/projr 90be50132d16aee33e39c0f7f35ef906c35f5397][r-root].
Rust comparison: [41cd7b2f][rust-root], plus the separate [CSV slice PR175][csv-pr].
This inventory was checked against dispatch, config parsing/defaults, store/restore
code, shipped template, documentation and test sources. R tests and live provider
operations were not executed for this audit. A test file is evidence of coverage
intent, not proof of a passing integration run.

**Current boundary:** local CAS export is implemented in Rust. Ordinary projr
latest/archive store/restore and GitHub Release-asset transport are still gaps.
CSV capture does not complete them or M2. CAS is an additional third structure,
not the replacement manifest format or the only archive layout.

## Providers, layouts and transports

| Surface | Actual pinned projr behaviour | projcli mapping and coverage |
|---|---|---|
| Provider/type enum | Only local and github are dispatched and validated. [Options][options], [dispatcher][dispatcher]. | Local CAS provider only; normal local and GitHub parity missing. Existing CAS integrity tests are not ordinary-remote tests. |
| Local | Plain filesystem directories/files; relative base is project root. No provider credentials. Lookup does not create directories. [Local][local]. | Local CAS path anchoring exists; latest/archive operations missing. |
| GitHub | GitHub Release assets via direct httr REST, with release tag + asset filename handles. Current implementation does not depend on piggyback despite comments. [GitHub][github], [HTTP][http]. | Missing. Git commit/push is a separate implemented feature, not Release-asset support. |
| OSF | Not in current enums/dispatch. Removed extra-option helper and explicit unsupported version helper remain. Old vignette mentions are stale. [Removed extras][dest], [OSF stub][versions]. | Do not advertise or implement merely from stale docs. |
| Other transports | No S3, generic HTTP-storage, SSH/SFTP or DVC provider in the dispatch. A local path can of course point to a mounted filesystem. [Options][options]. | No parity promise for absent providers. Future optional DVC remains separate. |
| latest hierarchy | Local path[/label]; label append defaults true. New sends update that location. [Layout][layout]. | Missing ordinary layout. |
| archive hierarchy | Local path[/label]/v&lt;version&gt;; versioned snapshots coexist. The remote pre-root holds shared metadata. [Layout][layout]. | Missing ordinary archive. Existing CAS snapshots do not establish this layout. |
| GitHub flat layout | Latest assets use path/label-derived flat name; archive adds version; ordinary content is ZIP-packaged. Metadata uses its own ZIP assets. [Flat naming][flat], [GitHub][github]. | Missing, including custom-prefix and append-label combinations. |
| Empty content | Local final name gets -empty; GitHub name gets -empty.zip and ZIP has projr-empty sentinel. Full/empty variants are reconciled. [Local][local], [store finalisation][store-final]. | CSV blank-filename marker is separate; remote empty representations missing. |
| CAS addition | Not an R layout. User requires it alongside latest and archive, with content-addressed versioned snapshots. | Existing local CAS objects/JSON/index are bounded groundwork; no new retention, GC or discovery policy adopted. |

## Configuration, defaults, aliases and precedence

R destinations are nested at build.local.&lt;title&gt; or build.github.&lt;title&gt;.
Directory sources live at directories.&lt;label&gt;.source, keyed by provider/title,
with string title references or inline mappings understood by restore helpers.
The source-selection helpers contain defects noted below; not every accepted
shape has demonstrated end-to-end behaviour. [Destination storage][dest],
[source getters][source], [restore selection][restore-select].

| Key or entrypoint | Parsed/defaulted/consumed behaviour | Rust status |
|---|---|---|
| Title | Named mapping key. Local helper describes title as descriptive; GitHub title becomes release tag. Internal title helper can derive it from content; public wrappers require the title argument. GitHub wrapper replaces spaces with hyphens. | Named CAS entries exist; release-tag resolution missing. |
| content | Validates allowed labels; send helper treats null/false as none, true as automatic output/raw/docs, vector as selected labels. Boolean helper support and strict validation are not fully consistent. Cache is not in automatic selection. | Explicit declared-label vector only. Boolean auto behaviour missing, subject to settled explicit-directory rules. |
| Special content | R option lists also mention docs/data/code/package; wrappers differ in their allowed sets, and code has special ZIP branches. This is not proof each implicit role works through all send paths. | Preserve approved output-r-data and explicit paths. Do not add implicit code/package/language roles merely from enum text; verify actual packaging route separately. |
| structure | archive by default; only archive/latest accepted. The wrapper prose saying version is not a supported alias. | cas only today; ordinary structures missing. |
| path | Required for local, anchored at project root when relative. Optional prefix for flat GitHub names. | CAS path is explicit/root-anchored; normal prefix rules missing. |
| path-append-label | Hyphenated YAML key; defaults true. Snake-case path_append_label is an R argument, not evidence of a YAML alias. | Missing. |
| id | Validator accepts it; completion overwrites local id with path and GitHub id with title. Do not mistake it for a freely configurable independent backend id. | No ordinary-remote id field. |
| description/id_parent/role | Internal add/check arguments include these legacy fields. Extra-options helper now discards OSF-related extras. No current standalone OSF behaviour follows. | No port required for dead fields without a working source route. |
| send.cue | if-change by default; enum only if-change/always. never occurs in stale wrapper docs but is rejected by current enum. Title-level cue lookup/setter and nested send.cue differ; see defects. | Missing. |
| send.inspect | manifest by default; file/manifest/none accepted. | CAS manifest/file checks exist but have different JSON/BLAKE3 meaning; none and ordinary MD5 comparison missing. |
| send.strategy | sync-diff default, except inspect:none defaults upload-all. Explicit upload-missing/upload-all/sync-purge/sync-diff preserved. | Missing ordinary strategies. |
| send.conflict | Validator accepts overwrite/skip/error, but no store consumer was found. | Accepted-only R surface, not a functioning conflict-policy requirement. Rust must not silently accept an ineffective control. |
| get.strategy/get.conflict | Accepted/checked; public destination wrappers comment out get arguments. Restore does not consume these policy fields. | Missing parser shape, but no implemented R policy to reproduce blindly. |
| source on destination | Restore permits true (preferred), false (exclude), or label vector (preferred for those labels); content must include the label. If absent, first eligible destination is fallback. | Missing ordinary source selection. |
| Per-directory source | Source lookup precedes destination lookup by default; pos can restrict source/dest, type and .title restrict selection. Inline/reference default paths are not uniformly reliable. | Missing. |
| Settings granularity | Transfer settings are shared per destination title; content labels inherit them. Per-label source mappings choose their own source entries. | CAS content entries share one inspect mode; ordinary resolved plans missing. |
| YAML layers | Local overrides active profiles overrides base; earlier listed profiles win; merge recurses, null inherits. R uses _projr base/profile/local names. [Merge][merge]. | Core merge precedence exists. Deliberate primary _proj.yml plus legacy _projr.yml conflict error retained. |
| Archive function arguments | archive_local/archive_github accept false/null, true or selected labels; create implicit archive destination only when YAML has no archive title. Existing archive title wins; always_archive controls generated cue. [Send dispatch][send]. | Missing compatibility entrypoints. Do not override explicit YAML silently. |
| Future registry | A separate user-requested registry/source-selection redesign is recorded; its naming remains open. | [Issue706][registry] is design-only; do not implement this new schema as part of parity work yet. |

## Store, inspection and metadata

Production/output builds only enter send; previews skip it. GitHub releases can
be prepared/created before analysis when configured. Destination parameters and
YAML are resolved per title, then labels are processed in content order. Source
files for a send come from the project's current-version manifest, not an
unqualified directory listing. The last label also triggers changelog writing.
[Preparation][prepare], [send][send], [planner][store].

| Policy | Implemented operation | Required Rust fixture |
|---|---|---|
| upload-all | Add every current source-manifest file; no removal of destination-only names. Existing destinations can be marked untrusted. | Existing extra file retained; source overwrite and empty-label cases. |
| upload-missing | Add names absent remotely; retain existing remote bytes, including changed same-name content. | Same-name different bytes retained; missing names added. |
| sync-diff | Add missing/changed files, remove remote-only files; compare via chosen inspection. | Add/change/delete transitions and no-change cue. |
| sync-purge | Clear/recreate destination content then upload full selected set when plan says needed. | Disposable fixture only; never user dataset destructive tests. |
| inspect:file | Enumerate/hash remote bytes with legacy MD5, compare to project evidence. | Detect actual byte corruption and ignore mtime/size equivalence. |
| inspect:manifest | Compare recorded rows/version trust. If unavailable/untrusted, planner may fall back to file hashes. | Matching/missing/stale/corrupt metadata and trust markers. |
| inspect:none | No comparison evidence; default upload-all and untrusted existing-state handling. | Never label unchecked remote bytes verified. |
| cue | always or change-driven materialisation/version updates; no trust or no prior destination can force creation. | Unchanged inputs under both cues; empty result snapshots. |
| Exclusions | Cache inventory excludes projr subtree. File listing includes dotfiles. ZIP helpers accept directory include/exclude and exact filename exclusions; filter implementations differ (pathspec vs regex). | Hidden files, nested names, exclusions and empty-after-exclusion; no regex/pathspec interchange assumption. |
| Execution | Purge, add, remove, reconcile full/empty, then write manifest, VERSION, and optional changelog. | Failure at each boundary must report partial publication honestly. |

[Plan execution][store-execute], [ZIP helpers][zip], [hashing][hash],
[listing/path filters][path].

Local metadata is ordinary manifest.csv, VERSION and CHANGELOG.md at the remote
pre-root. GitHub uses manifest.zip, VERSION.zip and CHANGELOG.zip containing those
files. VERSION has per-label release entries and optional trailing * indicating
untrusted state. These files are distinct from CAS JSON and the plural Rust
.projr/manifests.csv index. [Metadata][metadata].

There is no all-or-nothing remote transaction: local copying/removal can be
partial, GitHub whole-asset replacement deletes an old asset before uploading,
and metadata is written after content. Metadata-download failures may become
empty/unavailable state; some unzip errors are swallowed. Rust should retain
its approved safety boundaries, surface errors and never claim rollback of
remote side effects. [HTTP replacement][http-upload], [GitHub transfer][github].

## Versions, listing, downloads and restore

| Operation | Source behaviour | Rust comparison |
|---|---|---|
| List final remotes | Local immediate child directories; GitHub assets within one configured release. | Ordinary operations missing. No cross-release catalogue promised by R. |
| List files | Local recursive listing; GitHub ZIP download/extraction. | CAS manifests can list explicit entries internally; not these operations. |
| Latest version | latest reads label VERSION entry; archive parses local version-directory/GitHub asset names and selects max semantic version, including empty variants. | Read-only explicit local latest/archive listing is added in current source, with actual paths, empty variants and metadata markers. Automatic restore selection and GitHub discovery remain missing; current CAS accepts caller-supplied versions. |
| Trusted version | Stronger helper checks VERSION/archive agreement and project/remote manifest evidence. Restore bypasses this stronger helper. | Missing; do not describe ordinary restore as cryptographically verified. |
| Download all | Copy directory tree or download named release asset and unzip. | Missing ordinary download/restore. |
| Download one | Local and GitHub helpers flatten requested file to its basename at destination. | Missing; basename collision handling needs safe bounded implementation rather than unsafe silent overwrite. |
| Restore labels | Default declared raw labels; explicit labels supported. Root manifest required; empty/unrecorded labels may be skipped. | CSV prerequisite underway in PR175; restore absent. |
| Restore source | Source before destination; filter provider/title/content/source eligibility. First suitable selection, not retry across every provider after failure. Legacy fallback GitHub archive then local _archive exists. | Missing. |
| Restore target | Final declared path, safe=false; optional clear removes current contents before lookup/download. | Missing. Preserve guards; stage/validate before destructive promotion rather than importing unsafe legacy clearing. |
| Restore result | Per-label errors can yield partial false; clone wrapper can ignore that false and return true. | Must report failures honestly; do not preserve false success. |
| Clone wrapper | Clone repo, select/change working directory, invoke content update. | Existing Git-backed init is not a restore clone wrapper. |
| Most recently modified | Explicit unimplemented helpers; OSF variants explicitly unsupported. | Do not advertise working modification-time source selection. |

[Version logic][versions], [restore][restore], [clone wrappers][clone].

## Credentials and dependencies

GitHub lower helpers accept explicit token/api_url. Otherwise token lookup is
GITHUB_PAT, optional R gh::gh_token, optional gitcreds, GH_TOKEN, GITHUB_TOKEN.
API base is explicit override, GITHUB_API_URL, public API. Enterprise gitcreds
lookup strips /api/v3; public lookup uses https://github.com. Requests carry an
Authorization header and may be unauthenticated without a token. Repository
inference prefers origin then first Git remote, using available gh R helpers or
system Git/gert. Explicit Enterprise overrides are not forwarded by every wrapper.
[Authentication][auth], [repo inference][repo], [HTTP][http].

These are source mechanisms, not authorisation to obtain new credentials, change
permissions or install dependencies. Rust should use supported existing access,
mock HTTP for fixtures, redact secrets and never store tokens in CSV/URLs.
R helper auto-install behaviour is not adopted. Real Git remains an optional
installed dependency; GitHub CLI is separate and need not be mandatory for an
API implementation. Optional managed Git is not planned by default.

## Source defects and documentation-only surfaces

These are source-review findings, not executed reproductions or requirements to
copy bugs. Keep claims bounded until fixture evidence exists.

- Default source selection passes an inner mapping where the next helper expects
  the provider mapping; explicit provider selection can call a title-specific
  helper with a null title. [Selection][restore-select].
- GitHub existence checks hard-code label/version names, ignoring some custom
  path/append-label settings; local archive discovery assumes a label directory.
  [GitHub existence][github-exists], [version paths][versions].
- Title send-check reads top-level cue while defaults populate send.cue; the cue
  setter also writes a different level. [Send][send], [defaults][dest-default].
- get/conflict fields are validated but no effective execution consumer was
  found. wrapper docs mention never/version and OSF, outside actual enums.
- GitHub unzip failures can be swallowed, clone restore ignores partial failure,
  and low-level asset deletion can infer the current repo despite a repo argument.
  [GitHub][github], [HTTP][http], [clone][clone].
- Content option sets, wrapper checks and boolean auto-content helpers differ;
  special code/package labels alone do not prove working end-to-end export.


## Critical configuration assessment, separate from compatibility

This assessment excludes the agreed temporary CSV choice. Examples use the
existing R inline build configuration, not a newly approved Rust schema.
Findings are source-backed; unless stated otherwise they are not executed
reproductions. Proposed fixes are review candidates, not silent semantic changes.

| Rank/type | Example and user impact | Smallest proposed fix |
|---|---|---|
| High: ineffective accepted setting | A destination with send: {conflict: skip} passes allowed-value checks, but store execution never reads conflict. get: {strategy: upload-missing, conflict: error} similarly has no restore consumer. Users can believe a non-overwrite policy is enforced. [Checks][remote-check], [execution][store-execute]. | Reject ineffective combinations until implemented, or implement and test them explicitly. Do not silently ignore a safety control. |
| High: colliding-target combination | build.local.shared with content: [raw-a, raw-b], structure: latest, path-append-label: false, send: {inspect: file, strategy: sync-diff} gives both labels one physical directory. File inspection can classify the other label's files as extras. Custom archive/pre-root paths also assume layouts not uniformly supported. [Layout][layout], [planner][store], [versions][versions]. | Resolve all target identities before mutation and reject collisions; verify supported custom-prefix/append combinations rather than accepting untested layouts. |
| High: destructive restore ordering | A normal configured restore source plus projr_content_update(clear=TRUE) clears the destination before source resolution/download. A missing release or failed network call can leave data gone. clear defaults FALSE; this is an unsafe opt-in ordering, not an unsafe default. [Restore][restore]. | Download into private staging, validate, then apply guarded promotion. Preserve current data on lookup/download failure. |
| Medium: surprising default synchronisation | build.local.shared: {path: backup, structure: latest, content: [output]} defaults to sync-diff, so remote-only files can be removed. A user expecting an additive backup may be surprised. Default archive keeps prior version directories, which narrows the risk. [Defaults][dest-default], [planner][store]. | Clearly expose adds/removes and the resolved strategy before applying; require deliberate review before changing defaults. This is a usability/policy concern, not evidence that sync-diff itself is defective. |
| Medium: profile cannot disable with null | Base build.github.archive selects output; a local/profile build.github.archive: null inherits the base mapping. Removing one active-profile destination also does not remove its base definition. [Merge][merge]. | Explain merged effective destinations and provide a deliberately designed disabling/empty-selection mechanism. Do not reinterpret null without an approved compatibility change. |
| Medium: argument precedence surprise | YAML build.local.archive: {content: [raw-a], path: backup} means archive_local=c('raw-b') does not replace that archive definition. always_archive also defers to explicit archive YAML. [Dispatch][send]. | Document this as YAML authority and display the resolved content; avoid presenting these arguments as ordinary overrides. Whether arguments should override is a design choice. |
| Medium: two cue locations | send: {cue: always} is completed and used per label, while title-level send checking and the setter reference top-level cue. This invites inconsistent getter/setter behaviour; nested cue is not simply unused. [Send][send], [defaults][dest-default]. | Use one canonical nested location and test the public setter through an actual store plan; treat an alias only through explicit conflict rules. |
| Medium: provider-dependent identity | build.github.nightly: {id: another-tag, content: [output]} validates an id, but completion resets it to nightly. Local id instead becomes path. Title is cosmetic locally and functional on GitHub. [Completion][dest-default]. | Reject or clearly deprecate ignored id values; document title/tag/path meanings. A larger unified identity design is separate. |
| Medium: source-selection defects | directories.raw-data.source: {github: archive}, as shipped in the template, meets default helper paths that pass the wrong mapping level or an absent title into a title-specific branch. [Template][template], [selection][restore-select]. | Fix source selection with explicit/default provider/title fixtures; do not require users to discover accidental nesting workarounds. |
| Medium: unsupported documentation | send.cue: never and structure: version are mentioned in wrappers but excluded by current enums; old OSF prose outlives implementation. [Wrappers][wrappers], [enums][options]. | Correct docs and errors. Implement new values only if separately requested, not to make stale prose true. |
| Already recorded design | Removing a build destination can remove a historical restore source because definitions and upload selection share the same location. | The user-requested registry proposal is already [issue706][registry], design-only. It is not a new discovery here and is not implemented by this audit. |
| Low: naming preference | dest versus destinations changes readability, not provider or safety behaviour. | Choose during the existing registry discussion; no new alias or migration silently introduced. |

Credential lookup also deserves explicit presentation: ambient R gh/gitcreds
resolution precedes GH_TOKEN/GITHUB_TOKEN, and repository inference may choose
origin or the first remote. A supplied environment token or repository can
therefore differ from a user's expectation. The smallest safe improvement is
clear resolved host/repository diagnostics without secrets, plus tests for
explicit overrides; no new credential permissions are implied.

## Test evidence and bounded implementation sequence

[Test sources](https://github.com/SATVILab/projr/tree/90be50132d16aee33e39c0f7f35ef906c35f5397/tests/testthat)
were inspected without running R. Fixtures must establish behaviour before fixes
are claimed; a source test title alone is not an acceptance result.

| Source coverage | What it establishes here |
|---|---|
| test-yml-dest, test-yml-dest-wrapper, test-yml-remote-check | Parser/default/helper assertions exist, including accepted values. Not run in this audit. |
| test-dest-send, test-dest-send-label, test-dest-send-prepare | Dispatch/planner/version/empty helper coverage exists. Not whole-provider publication evidence. |
| test-remote-dispatcher, test-remote-local, test-remote-versions-local | Local dispatcher/layout/transfer/version fixtures exist. Reproduce equivalent Rust fixtures remotely. |
| test-remote-github | Tests require mutable credentials and explicitly skip GitHub Actions. Presence is not CI coverage. Prefer safe mocked REST/ZIP fixtures for Rust. |
| test-restore, test-restore-coverage, test-restore-repo | Restore selection/validation/clone test intent; source defects above still require targeted witnesses. |
| Existing Rust CAS tests | Prove bounded BLAKE3 object/JSON/index behaviour, not ordinary latest/archive parity. |
| PR175 CSV tests | Production pre/post MD5/history, strict encoding, exclusions and recovery; separate exact-head CI/review evidence on that PR. |

Next slices should remain independently testable:

1. Read-only ordinary local latest/archive inspection is the current bounded
   source slice: [command reference](cli/remote.qmd), explicit paths and empty
   variants. It introduces no remote registry schema; exact-head remote checks
   and independent review are required before merge.
2. Current source adds explicit file-inspected plans/execution for the four
   strategies; configured inspection/cue/metadata publication remains missing.
3. Explicit local download is the next bounded source slice, using staged
   destination replacement and honest outcomes; configured restore remains open.
4. GitHub REST/ZIP transport behind mock fixtures, existing credential lookup,
   release/asset/version/metadata behaviour and failure reporting; no live dataset uploads.
5. Cross-provider source selection and configuration compatibility, preserving
   confirmed aliases and resolving source bugs with regression evidence.
6. CAS-specific archive integration only where existing structures do not decide
   snapshot discovery/retention. Those choices must not block ordinary parity.

The full inventory stays open until implemented and independently reviewed
evidence maps every supported row. CSV completion alone closes none of the
broader provenance/remote milestones. The future registry proposal is separate
planned work; do not silently implement it while porting old inline definitions.

## Explicit GitHub Release asset transport

The source candidate adds native HTTPS REST asset listing, new uploads and
staged downloads through remote github assets/upload/download. It preserves
Enterprise API base paths and exact Release tags, lists paginated assets, and
strips authentication from binary redirects. Uploads require an existing token;
duplicate asset names fail without deleting the old asset. Release creation is
explicit. Downloads require an explicit byte limit and protect project authority
files, links and special entries, preserving old bytes on incomplete transfers.
Network failures after upload may leave an uncertain remote result; inspect it
before retrying. No credential installation or live-data test is authorised.

Tokens use GITHUB_PAT, then GH_TOKEN, then GITHUB_TOKEN. GITHUB_API_URL selects
the API base. Git credential helpers and gh-token fallback remain unported here.
Listing/downloading public assets can be anonymous. Literal loopback HTTP is
accepted for disposable fixtures; ordinary service URLs require HTTPS.

This is the actual transport prerequisite for existing projr GitHub latest/archive
support, not complete configured publication/restore. ZIPs are opaque in this
slice; packaging, projr names, VERSION/manifest/CHANGELOG ZIP metadata, replacement
policy and configured restore remain subsequent work. No registry/CAS redesign.
Pinned comparison: remote-github-httr.R REST transport and remote-github.R ZIP
transfer at 90be50132d16aee33e39c0f7f35ef906c35f5397.

Ponytail full: one concrete HTTP client and an established synchronous HTTPS
crate rather than a provider trait, GitHub CLI dependency or custom TLS. Reuse
existing path guards and tempfile replacement. Mocked local HTTP fixture tests
exercise real requests/bodies and CLI JSON without live GitHub writes. No local
compilation/tests run; remote exact-head compilation, locked/API/docs/acceptance
and independent review are still required. Source candidate is not installed.

The CLI does not initialise HTTP wire logging and its own error messages omit
tokens, response bodies and signed redirect URLs. Library embedders must avoid
ureq DEBUG/TRACE logging for sensitive requests because dependency logging is
not redacted. Redirects remove Authorization but do not confine network access
to a provider host; this transport is not a network sandbox.


## GitHub ZIP packaging and explicit directory transfer candidate

This candidate extends the native Release transport with projr flat names:
prefix-label-vVERSION.zip for archive, prefix-label.zip for latest, and
-empty before .zip for empty variants. With no prefix, the label is always
used, including path_append_label=false. Metadata assets remain shared and
unprefixed: manifest.zip contains manifest.csv, VERSION.zip contains VERSION,
and CHANGELOG.zip contains CHANGELOG.md. Directory ZIP entries are relative to
the selected source, without an enclosing folder. Nonempty parent-directory entries retain Unix
permission modes; empty directory entries remain omitted. Empty sources contain the
single zero-byte projr-empty sentinel; empty subdirectories are not archived.

The CLI adds remote github upload-directory (label/structure/remote-version,
optional prefix/path-append-label), upload-metadata (kind manifest/version/
changelog and a source directory), and download-directory (exact asset name,
destination, max-bytes, max-expanded-bytes, optional clear/empty). Uploads remain
new-name-only; metadata is packaged byte-for-byte rather than silently merged.
Download stages extraction privately and uses the existing guarded merge/clear
installer. Explicit empty requires exactly the sentinel and consumes it before
installation. Destination-only files survive unless clear is requested.

Safety changes from R's direct utils::unzip: bounded expanded bytes and100000
members, CRC validation, reject links/special/encrypted entries, traversal,
backslashes, device names, native aliases, duplicate members and parent/file
collisions before project installation. Retain existing installer rollback and
Windows backup-cleanup limits; no crash/concurrent-writer guarantee is added.

Ponytail full: one ZIP crate with only Deflate enabled, existing MD5 inventory,
HTTP client and guarded installer. No backend interface, registry or new YAML
policy. Independent tests cover exact metadata/Unicode/hidden/empty members,
malicious names, CRC/expanded limits and mocked actual ZIP upload/download
merge/clear. No local heavy tests; remote lock resolution, exact-head platform/
pinned/docs acceptance and independent review are pending.

Pinned sources:
[flat names](https://github.com/SATVILab/projr/blob/90be50132d16aee33e39c0f7f35ef906c35f5397/R/remote.R#L525),
[ZIP layout](https://github.com/SATVILab/projr/blob/90be50132d16aee33e39c0f7f35ef906c35f5397/R/misc.R#L638),
[empty sentinel](https://github.com/SATVILab/projr/blob/90be50132d16aee33e39c0f7f35ef906c35f5397/R/remote-github.R#L350),
[metadata assets](https://github.com/SATVILab/projr/blob/90be50132d16aee33e39c0f7f35ef906c35f5397/R/remote-versions.R#L1).
Configured source selection/restore, historical metadata merging, latest asset
replacement, credentials-helper fallback and CAS remain outstanding. This
source candidate does not update the published/installed preview.

Review amendments share the existing native directory-entry alias guard with
file-policy transfers, validate empty-directory CRC with a bounded probe, and
never persist an expanded-byte probe beyond each member's advertised size.
Directory modes apply deepest-first after extraction; an existing destination's
modes still follow the previously documented merge policy. File-only ZIPs from
other writers have no directory privacy metadata to restore. Source root modes
are not encoded as a new manifest field. No ACL/ownership/xattr claim follows.
Temporary paths are created beneath the physical canonical system temp directory;
macOS /var aliases are not an excuse to weaken external path guards.

Extraction also checks actual directory spelling immediately after creation,
rejecting filesystems that rewrite it rather than merging distinct Unicode
members. The extracted-tree owner restores directory owner access for cleanup;
explicit close reports a retained path on cleanup failure. The directory-transfer
command checks extraction and transfer cleanup on success and failure and
distinguishes installed output from failed transfer. Readonly/zero-mode owned
directory cleanup is exercised unprivileged in the pinned gate.


## Explicit GitHub asset replacement

The source candidate adds --replace to upload, upload-directory and upload-metadata,
and GithubReleaseClient::replace_asset. Default uploads still reject existing
names. Explicit replacement follows the working projr delete-then-upload sequence:
[remote-github-httr.R554-662](https://github.com/SATVILab/projr/blob/90be50132d16aee33e39c0f7f35ef906c35f5397/R/remote-github-httr.R#L554).

Before deletion, validate the regular source, stage its complete bytes privately,
resolve the Release/unique asset and validate its trusted upload endpoint. An
absent name uploads normally. A successful delete is followed by one upload;
errors after deletion explicitly state that the previous asset was deleted.
An interrupted deletion reports an uncertain old-asset state and does not start
the upload. This is not atomic publication, backup retention or remote rollback.
There is no automatic retry, new history/sealing policy or changed YAML default.

Ponytail full reuses the existing client and request/body fixtures, with a private
file snapshot only for explicit replacement. Mocked end-to-end witnesses cover
staged bytes despite source mutation after delete, exact DELETE/POST ordering,
denied/interrupted delete, failed/malformed upload, untrusted endpoints, ambiguous
names, unsafe sources and machine CLI output. These are mocked REST operations,
not actual GitHub Release mutations. No live user data/credentials or local
heavy tests. Remote exact-head gates and independent review remain required.
Configured restore/source selection and full automatic publication remain next.
